_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. These are governance-tier hand-corrections: onboard.py --resume preserves governance.md, but a FULL reprint re-runs gen_governance.py and would re-introduce the mis-tiering.

handfixes.summary: Write tier unions the keyword-matched mutations (incl. `agents update`) WITH the verb-less writes (`import`) and inspection triggers (`launchpoints run`/`bulk-run`)
handfixes.why: gen_governance.py keyword-matches command paths and ignores pp:method. It correctly placed `agents update` (a real PUT) in Write but missed verb-less/action writes (`import` bulk upsert, the inspection triggers `launchpoints run`/`bulk-run`/`run-stale`, `agents flush job-queue`). When hand-adding the verb-less writes you must UNION (keep `agents update`), not replace - a prior draft dropped `agents update` so it fell into NO tier and an agent following SKILL.md routing would run a config write ungated (round-1 adversarial P1). A full reprint re-runs gen_governance and re-introduces both the drop risk and the missing verb-less writes. See project_governance_rewrite_union_not_replace, project_gen_governance_misses_verbless_writes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Make gen_governance method-aware off agent-context pp:method (fleet-wide). Until then this hand-correction recurs on every reprint.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For liongard the manifest gained: LIONGARD_BASE_URL. server.json gained: LIONGARD_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: LIONGARD_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: config.Load composes LIONGARD_ACCESS_KEY_ID + LIONGARD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET into the base64 X-ROAR-API-KEY value when LIONGARD_API_KEY is unset; the ID, the secret, the id:secret pair and the composed header are held the moment they are derived, and an unresolved .mcpb placeholder is never a credential (EnvOverride)
handfixes.why: Liongard hands an operator two separate strings - an Access Key ID and an Access Key Secret - and never shows the encoded form. The wire header X-ROAR-API-KEY is base64("accessKeyId:accessKeySecret"), so the CLI has to compose it. README.md, SKILL.md, guide.md and server.json all instruct operators to export the two variables. The press template emits a single-env-var loader (one variable per config field) and has no notion of a composed credential, so a reprint or a fleet re-vendor regenerates config.go and drops the composed branch: the 4.24.0 fleet re-vendor (fc7720092) did exactly that, and from then on every operator who followed the shipped docs got an empty auth header and a 401 on every call while the connector's own hand-added test (config_liongard_auth_test.go) failed in CI. The branch is inline in a DO-NOT-EDIT generated file, so this ledger entry is the only thing that makes the next drop loud. Same class as the levelio x-auth-env-vars regression and gradient's composed GRADIENT-TOKEN pair (which survives reprints only because it lives in a novel file). 4.34.2 reprint: re-applied by an anchored script (reapply: tools/apply_edits.py in the run dir) over the fresh config.go, reading the pair through cliutil.EnvOverride, holding every derived form for the output chokepoint, and counting the pair as an environment credential for the untrusted-config refusal (envHasCredential).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Teach the press composed-credential auth (N env vars -> one derived header value) so the loader is generated, not hand-wired. Until then this recurs on every reprint.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: agents flush job-queue (POST /agents/{AgentID}/flush).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: Every resource write passes mergeIncomingResourceData, which returns withoutStoredSecrets of the record: a value under a declared credential response field (store.CredentialResponseFields, the names credwire declares as ResponseFields, SecureConfig and Secrets included) is replaced by "[redacted]" at any depth, so the record stays storable. A held value anywhere else in a statement is refused by the kit (credkit-sqlite-every-handle).
handfixes.why: Work order: no credential in files. The kit's SQL driver refuses a statement that carries a held value, which would drop a whole launchpoint listing whose SecureConfig holds a credential; redacting the declared names first keeps the record. Replaces the connector-only storedID and WithholdingSQLiteDriver.

handfixes.summary: export --output closes its (withholding) output file on every return, including an API error: the open no longer shadows RunE's named err
handfixes.why: The generated `f, err := openExportOutput(...)` inside the --output block declared a new err, so the deferred close tested that inner (nil) err and never ran when the export returned an API error. With the output chokepoint the file is a filter pipe, and the unclosed pipe kept the process from exiting: `export clients --output f.jsonl` after a 401 hung (TestExportOutputReturnsAfterAnAPIError, seen failing 3 of 4 runs). Fleet note: every connector that took the ported chokepoint edit on export.go carries the same shadowing. Ported to liongard from the gradient 4.34.2 reprint (one credential layer across the fleet).

handfixes.summary: The X-ROAR-API-KEY and X-Auth-Token headers and every API request go only to the scheme, host and port of the RESOLVED per-instance base URL (https://{instance}.app.liongard.com/api/v1 with LIONGARD_INSTANCE, or LIONGARD_BASE_URL); every redirect hop must stay on that origin, a non-ASCII host never matches, and an unresolved or unparseable base URL pins nothing (every request refused). Installed on every CLI, novel and MCP client by registerClientHook (internal/cli/liongard_guard.go), with the response cache off and --dry-run clients refusing every send
handfixes.why: Credential rule host pinning: the generated client sends the credential header to whatever URL it is handed and its CheckRedirect strips only the named auth headers. Liongard's base URL is a template, and url.Parse refuses the raw `{instance}` host, so the pin is taken from client.ResolvedBaseURL(c.BaseURL, c.CurrentTemplateVars()); pinning the raw template would refuse every request, pinning nothing would follow any redirect. Kept beside the shared credential kit: the kit refuses a held value to any other origin, but lets an uncredentialed request go anywhere, so the pin still keeps every API request on the resolved instance; the kit's Transport (client.OutboundGuard) runs under it.

handfixes.why: The mirror confirm gate's own `confirm` argument shadows the novel's --confirm flag of the same name and is stripped before the child runs, so the bulk inspection kick could only ever plan over MCP (confirm: true ran the plan again). handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own holder, funnel, output chokepoint, outbound checks and SQLite wrapper. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; the API client goes through credkit.Transport under the origin pin, as do the feedback, --deliver webhook and probe clients; every file write except config.toml and the 0600 credential store (sources, listed in Declarations.Files) goes through the kit; MCP stdio, tools and child processes go through the kit; stdout and stderr are the kit's pipes.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring. Liongard's base URL is a template (https://{instance}.app.liongard.com/api/v1) the kit cannot parse, so credentialFiles shows the kit the URL the client really resolves (config.Load under this command line, then client.ResolvedBaseURL, the call the origin pin makes) through LIONGARD_BASE_URL for the duration of Start, and AfterStart puts the variable back. With no instance (the placeholder "example") or a template left unfilled, the kit is shown the shipped template, which does not parse, so no origin is allowed and every credentialed request is refused. Saved profiles are held at startup. Tests: internal/credwire (TestShownBaseURLIsTheResolvedInstance, TestAfterStartRestoresTheBaseURL, TestUnresolvedBaseURLAllowsNoOrigin), internal/liongardblackbox (kit_classes_test.go, TestSavedProfileCredentialHeld, the four-mode batteries). The three variable-path reads in hand-edited code (the data.db.owner marker in helpers.go, the journal tail, the profile store) take filepath.Clean, which is the security gate's sanitizer for G304, so no inline suppression is needed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the credkit wiring from a per-connector declarations file, and let a declaration name a templated base URL resolved with its template variables, so a reprint keeps it by construction.

handfixes.why: A base URL may carry userinfo, and config.toml is a credential source the kit holds at startup. handfixes.summary: The learn journal and teach log keep no credential: the LIONGARD_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash harness session ids get under "h:" (sessions still group); argv_shape records a flag name only when the invoked command's declared-flag lookup declares it exactly as typed (every other name, and every name when no lookup is given, is the "<undeclared>" placeholder) and reads nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>" when a suggestion paired it, otherwise dropped); every file this package writes (journal entry, tail repair, derivation offset, teach.log) goes through the shared credential kit (credkit.AppendFile / credkit.WriteFile), which withholds a held credential in any field. journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path with a credential, not held and held, and fails if any 8-character piece of it reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 learn/journal.go.tmpl returns the LEARN_SESSION override raw from JournalSessionKey (written to journal-*.jsonl on every command) and records every typed flag name (a credential typed as a flag name, or after --, became an argv_shape key and the failed_flag); journal.go and teach_log.go wrote with os.OpenFile/AtomicWritePrivateFile outside the kit. The ported output layer (cliutil.WithholdBytes in teach_log.go) is replaced by the kit route. Known limits: a guessable override can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening.

handfixes.why: Synced metric definitions carry no values (Liongard evaluates them per system through /metrics/bulk), so the old text promised a value table and a threshold scan the binary cannot give from local data. guide.md and SKILL.md are re-vendored by onboard.py from the press output, which carries the old wording.

handfixes.summary: access-keys delete's pp:happy-args sample uses AccessKeyID=101 instead of the spec's 20-character example ID.
handfixes.why: gitleaks' generic-api-key rule reads `AccessKeyID=<20 random-looking chars>` as a leaked key and fails the repo's secret scan; the sample only feeds offline dogfood/verify calls, so a short numeric ID proves the same thing. The press regenerates the spec example on a reprint.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored, sync keeps walking, and the run still succeeds, naming the row ids on stderr and in its summary
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows). synccpu (2026-11-09): a withheld row no longer fails the resource. mcp2 measured hubspot-calls-crm row 80663490159 turning the whole sync into exit 1, so the server never marked the connector synced. Now the resource ends stored with the ids named (stderr warning, a sync_warning rows_withheld event per page, and "withheld" in the summary), the run exits 0 when every other row stored, and the resource's checkpoint stays where the attempt began so the next run fetches the row again.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync_progress reports measured rows per second (rows_per_sec, and rate_rps as the same value); the limiter's ceiling is limiter_ceiling_rps.
handfixes.why: The generated sync printed the adaptive limiter's ceiling as rate_rps and as req/s on the human line, so 4.9 was reported while the sync stored 33 rows a second (#694). A reprint regenerates sync.go and brings it back; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-measured-rate).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template should report a measured rate and name the limiter's ceiling separately (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: sync writes at most one sync_progress line per resource every 5 seconds (the first page always reports; sync_complete carries the final count), instead of one per page.
handfixes.why: Every write to stdout or stderr costs a full credential check whatever its size, and sync wrote one progress line per page: 74% of hubspot sync's CPU at a real server's pace (#696). A reprint regenerates sync.go with one line per page; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies the guard (fleet_handfixes.json sync-progress-throttled).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the sync template's per-page progress line should be throttled, as its dependent walk already is (not filed yet).

handfixes.summary: The <api>_search tool's description ends with the API's resource families (codeOrchSearchResources in internal/mcp/search_desc.go, from codeOrchEndpoints, capped at 300 characters).
handfixes.why: The generated description was the same in every connector and named no resource, so a host that ranks tools by words put other tools above <api>_search for "<api> <resource>" (#629; zammad_search ranked 13th of 45 for "zammad tickets"). A reprint regenerates code_orch.go without the call; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json mcp-search-desc-resources).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (upstream PR named in fleet_handfixes.json): the code-orchestration template should build the <api>_search description from the endpoint registry's resource families.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
